# Canary

Updated: 2026-11-03 08:40 CET. Current release: v3.32.1.

Canary is a local risk desk for an Interactive Brokers account. One daemon
on the user's machine reads a running IB Gateway or TWS session and serves
the same evidence to four adapters: a shell CLI, a read-only MCP server, a
paired phone app and a Go client. It is a private open-source project by one
maintainer, MIT licensed, with no hosted service and no telemetry.

This file is the map. The release history, tool list and command list are
in https://osauer.dev/canary/llms-full.txt.

## Who it is for

An IBKR Pro user who runs Gateway or TWS locally and wants stale, missing or
held evidence to stay visible. It is not a hosted brokerage service, a trade
recommender or a complete TWS API replacement. macOS and Linux on arm64 or
amd64; Windows through WSL only.

## Two builds, one boundary

Canary reads the account, and in the trading build it also executes the
orders the owner authorised. The standard binary has no compiled order path.
The separate `canary-trading` binary places a transaction the owner
confirmed, or a close or reduction the daemon runs under a bucket listed in
the owner's written policy; every order is pinned to one account, client ID
and mode, consumes a preview token for that draft, is journaled before the
send, and passes the risk policy's order limits, the mandate gate and the
freeze. An agent trades only through the gated CLI. No MCP tool can preview
or execute an order in any build; an assistant that tries to trade through
`canary mcp` has reached outside the tool's capability boundary. Canary never
decides a trade on its own.

## Surfaces

- MCP: `canary mcp` over stdio, or the Claude Desktop bundle `canary.mcpb`.
  Read-only tools for status, account, positions, brief, rules, regime,
  stress, reporting, lending, short interest, Edge, calendars and orders.
  Reference: https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/reference/mcp-tools.html
- CLI: `canary brief`, `canary positions --by underlying`, `--json` on every
  read. Reference: https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/reference/cli.html
- App: `canary app`, then `canary app pair`; local by default, optional relay.
  https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/operate/app.html
- Go: `github.com/osauer/canary/v2` is the daemon client, `canarytest` its
  test double, `pkg/ibkr` the TWS wire protocol. The module stays on `/v2`;
  product v3 tags do not change it. https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/osauer/canary/v2

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osauer/canary/main/install.sh | sh
canary status
canary brief
```

The installer verifies the signed release checksum and installs to
`~/.local/bin`. Hosts: https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/start/hosts.html

## Where things live in the repository

- `AGENTS.md`: the contracts an agent reads before changing behaviour, with
  a table of which document governs which area. `.agents/docs/` holds them:
  the daemon and CLI trading contract, the risk policy contract, the MCP
  description guide, the SPA authority matrix, the release procedure.
- `internal/daemon` owns broker state; `internal/risk` owns risk semantics;
  `internal/rpc` owns the cross-surface contracts. `internal/cli`,
  `internal/mcp` and `internal/app` are adapters and may not persist state.
- `pkg/ibkr` is the broker layer in its own package so other brokers can
  follow. `cmd/canary` is the binary.
- `docs/docs/` is the handbook in Markdown: `start/` (install, first
  session, hosts, reporting, troubleshooting), `operate/` (daily desk,
  alerts, protection, orders, reconciliation, agents), `understand/`
  (concepts, rulebook, risk policy, sensors, market data, Edge),
  `reference/` (generated CLI, MCP and config references), `internals/`
  (architecture, protocol, storage).
- Generated references are regenerated with `make docs-regen` and checked
  by `make check`. Human-readable CLI output has golden render tests in
  `internal/cli`.

## How to contribute, and where to file what

Read `CONTRIBUTING.md` in full. In short:

- Issues labelled `help wanted` or `good first issue` are reserved for
  outside contributors for seven days. Every other issue is the maintainer's
  defect log and may be fixed within the hour.
- A first pull request references a reserved issue or changes documentation,
  help text or error wording. Risk semantics, limits, freeze and the gated
  order path change only after a policy discussion.
- Run `make check` before opening a pull request and quote its last line.
- Agent-authored work is welcome when a person stands behind it and signs
  the CLA; that person is the author of record.
- Never include account ids, balances, positions, order references,
  hostnames or home paths, in prose, fixtures or screenshots.

File a reproducible defect as an issue: https://github.com/osauer/canary/issues/new/choose
Anything that carries account or gateway detail goes by email instead:
https://osauer.dev/canary/feedback/#private
Security problems: https://github.com/osauer/canary/blob/main/SECURITY.md

## What not to claim about Canary

It reports the evidence currently available and names what is stale,
degraded, held, blocked or unknown. Do not say a delayed value is live, that
an MCP client has order authority, that a plan or proposal row is an order,
that Edge forecasts or proves causation, or that a v3 product tag makes the
Go module v3.
